svg.title: Numerical and exact greedy decision gates with near tie example
svg.desc: Every finite aligned coordinate must satisfy its predeclared mixed absolute relative allowance. A constructed near tie changes greedy winner from zero to one with only two times ten to the minus eleven maximum error, passing the score screen but failing exact decision agreement. Matching selected IDs may conversely hide wrong logits. Both gates are required.
svg.text: Score closeness and greedy agreement are separate gates
Numerical gate: every finite coordinate fits its declared allowance
Also require aligned shapes, vocabulary, positions and state identities.
Near tie: score screen passes while greedy changes
Maximum coordinate error: 2 × 10⁻¹¹. Constructed comparator example.
Exact greedy gate: same IDs, visible prefixes and terminal result
Matching IDs can also hide wrong logits: the frozen-prompt fault does so.
A pass on one gate never substitutes for the other.
Sufficient winner condition with uniform error ε: reference gap Δ > 2ε.
